candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — apply infection-prevention and PPE practices and adapt safety measures to resource and environmental conditions while protecting clients and health care personnel.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE shortage surge-capacity strategies
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish crisis-capacity PPE strategies from conventional and contingency approaches: crisis measures are temporary, higher-risk options for known shortages when supply cannot meet current utilization and should end as adequate supply returns.

options.A: Continue crisis-capacity practices as the routine standard after PPE availability again meets facility needs.
options.B: Move directly to crisis-capacity practices when a future shortage is only anticipated but current PPE supply still meets utilization.
options.C: Use crisis-capacity practices whenever future supply adequacy is uncertain, even before contingency strategies are considered.
options.D: Use crisis-capacity practices temporarily during a known shortage when PPE supply cannot meet current utilization, after considering conventional and contingency approaches.

candidate.rationale: CDC/NIOSH describes three surge-capacity strata. Conventional practices are routine; contingency strategies may be used temporarily during anticipated shortages or uncertainty about future supply; crisis-capacity strategies are higher-risk measures that may be used temporarily during known PPE shortages when supply cannot meet the facility's current utilization rate. Conservation strategies are meant to be considered sequentially, and facilities should promptly resume conventional practices as PPE availability improves. Therefore D is correct. A incorrectly makes crisis practices routine after recovery, while B and C apply crisis measures to circumstances that CDC/NIOSH describes as contingency rather than crisis capacity.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Crisis-capacity PPE strategies are temporary higher-risk measures for known shortages when supply cannot meet current utilization; they follow consideration of lower-risk capacity strategies and should be discontinued as adequate supply returns.
candidate.source_document_title: Conserving Supplies of Personal Protective Equipment in Healthcare Facilities during Shortages
candidate.source_locator: Surge capacity: definitions of Conventional capacity, Contingency capacity, and Crisis capacity. Crisis capacity: temporary during known PPE shortages when supply cannot meet current utilization; highest risk; not routine replacement. PPE supply conservation strategies: contingency then crisis strategies augment conventional strategies and are meant to be considered sequentially; promptly resume standard conventional practices as PPE availability increases.
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
candidate.stem: Which statement best describes crisis-capacity PPE strategies during a severe shortage?
